subject: Physics
title: Speed vs Velocity
summary: Two cars at the same 60 km/h can have different velocities. Speed tells how fast; velocity also tells which way.
keyPoints: Constant speed on a circle → **changing velocity** (direction changes).
SI unit of both: **m/s**; 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s.

blocks.p: Two cars on a highway both read **60 km/h**. One heads east, the other west. Their **speed** is the same, but their **velocity** is not, because velocity includes the **direction** of motion.

blocks.alt: Two cars at 60 km/h, one going east and one going west
blocks.caption: Same speed, opposite directions: different velocities.

blocks.p: **Distance** is the length of the actual path. **Displacement** is the straight arrow from start to finish, with a direction. Speed is built on distance; velocity is built on displacement.

blocks.alt: A wiggly path from A to B with a straight displacement arrow
blocks.caption: Orange: the path (distance). Purple: the displacement.

blocks.formula: Speed = distance ÷ time      Velocity = displacement ÷ time

sections.h: The twist: constant speed, changing velocity

blocks.p: A car going round a circular track at a steady 60 km/h never changes its **speed**, but its **direction** changes at every moment, so its **velocity keeps changing**. This is uniform circular motion, an accelerated motion.

blocks.alt: Velocity arrows tangent to a circle at four points
blocks.caption: Velocity is always along the tangent; its direction keeps turning.

sections.h: Speed vs velocity at a glance

quiz.q: Which of these is a vector quantity?
quiz.explain: Velocity has both size and direction, so it is a vector. Speed, distance and time have size only.

quiz.q: Two buses both move at 40 km/h, one north and one south. Which statement is true?
quiz.explain: The speeds are equal (40 km/h), but the directions are opposite, so the velocities are different.

quiz.q: A car goes round a circular track at a constant 60 km/h. Its velocity:
options: keeps changing because its direction changes
equals its speed at every moment, so it does not change
quiz.explain: The size stays 60 km/h, but the direction changes all the time, so the velocity changes. That is uniform circular motion.

quiz.q: A girl walks 30 m east and then 30 m back west in 20 s. Her average velocity is:
quiz.explain: She ends where she started, so her displacement is 0 and her average velocity is 0 m/s. (Her average speed is 60 m ÷ 20 s = 3 m/s.)

simulation.reason: Students benefit from moving an object along different paths and watching distance vs displacement, and speed vs velocity, diverge; the circular track shows the velocity arrow turning at constant speed - cause and effect that a fixed video cannot let them test.
simulation.objective: See when speed and velocity agree, when they differ, and why constant speed on a circle still means changing velocity.
instructions: Pick a path: straight, there-and-back, zig-zag or circle.
Press Play (or drag the time slider) and watch the distance and the displacement arrow.
Compare the average speed and the average velocity readouts.
On the circle, watch the purple velocity arrow turn while the speed stays the same.
